subject: NimbleCart QPS variance — triage, product asks, and customer brief
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@nimblecart.com>, ops@nimblecart.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-12-07T08:12:00Z
Subject: [ALERT] Spike in QPS variance impacting NimbleCart gen endpoints

Team — quick heads up. We started seeing a sharp variance in request queue lengths for NimbleCart between 07:48 and 08:05 PST. Symptoms observed:
- p95 latency for /v1/generate rose from ~180ms to 1.2s for a sustained 10m window.
- throughput (tokens/s) dropped ~28% on a subset of their traffic (2 of 6 routes).
- KV cache miss rate spiked for long prompt prefixes.

I attached a lightweight CSV with aggregated metrics and a minimal trace set (tail-traces-20261207.json). Initial notes from the runtime: unusual fanout (many short-lived parallel calls) + a sudden increase in sequence length variance. Suspecting a combination of small-batch inefficiency and route-specific scheduling hot-spot.

Immediate asks:
1) Product: advise on whether we can propose a short-term routing policy exception (prefer low-latency lanes) for NimbleCart traffic.
2) Eng/SRE (Karthik/Marissa): prioritize short traces and a recommended mitigation (e.g., force single-shard affinity for the affected routes).
3) CS (Jasmine): prepare a concise customer note — what happened, what we’re doing, ETA for next update. Keep it non-technical.

Impact: NimbleCart reports a mild increase in end-user latencies; they are seeing elevated error logs but not full outages. I marked JIRA PERF-4821 and copied a Drive link.

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: latency-sample-20261207.csv (text/csv), tail-traces-20261207.json (application/json)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@nimblecart.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T08:35:00Z
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Spike in QPS variance impacting NimbleCart gen endpoints

On Mon, Dec 7, 2026 at 08:12 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — quick heads up. We started seeing a sharp variance in request queue lengths for NimbleCart...

Thanks Ben — triage notes below.
- I confirmed a ~30% increase in small-batch occupancy (N=1-3) for route /v1/generate/checkout which is inefficient on current scheduler.
- Node-level load shows two hosts with repeated long-tail KV cache misses (likely cache evaporation during short-lived flows).
- No memory leaks or GPU saturations observed.

Short mitigations I can run now:
A) Toggle affinity for the route to the low-latency pool (will reduce cold-starts but inch cost up). Needs product approval.
B) Enforce a soft rate-limit per-tenant burst window to flatten fanout (UC of 30s). This we can gate in runtime quickly.

I can flip (B) in the next 20m and monitor. If product approves A, I’ll coordinate with infra to schedule it (10–15m to converge).

Marissa
Tech Lead, Serving Runtime

Attachments: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Spike in QPS variance impacting NimbleCart gen endpoints — short technical summary

Marissa — thanks for the triage. Technical addenda for the product/CS crowd: 
- Root cause hypothesis: workload pattern changed at customer side — higher variance in sequence length + more concurrent short-lived requests leading to scheduler fragmentation and higher per-token overhead.
- Risk of immediate fix (A: affinity to low-latency pool): forces traffic onto fewer nodes; lowers tail latency BUT reduces headroom for other customers on that pool. We should set a temporary guardrail (max 10% capacity reservation).
- Proposed step 1 (fast, low risk): enable the runtime soft rate-limit (Marissa B) and increase prefix-KV retention for NimbleCart routes for 15m.
- Proposed step 2 (if problem persists >30m): grant a routing exception to low-latency pool with capacity reservation and notify Sales/Finance for bookkeeping.

I’ve uploaded a small trace bundle to the Drive link and created a minimal runbook task list in JIRA PERF-4821 (items: monitor p95, toggle rate-limit, change affinity, revert).

Karthik
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: tail-traces-20261207.json

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-07T10:02:00Z
Subject: Customer update: brief on current NimbleCart performance variance (non-technical)

Alex — following up with a short, non-technical note to explain what we’re doing and when you’ll hear next from us. Please feel free to push back on tone/ask.

--- customer note (draft) ---
Hi Alex / NimbleCart Ops,

We saw a temporary increase in request processing times that affected a subset of your traffic this morning. Our engineering team identified the likely cause and have already implemented an initial mitigation (small request smoothing). We are monitoring closely and expect to have a clearer status and next update within 30 minutes.

What we did so far:
- Applied a short-term smoothing rule to reduce bursts and stabilize latency.
- Collected traces and metrics to pinpoint the root cause.

What’s next:
- If the issue is not fully resolved within 30 minutes, we will move traffic to a low-latency pool under a temporary routing exception while preserving capacity safeguards.
- We will share a short incident summary and recommended long-term changes (e.g., batching suggestions) after the immediate triage.

We apologize for the disruption — our priority is restoring consistent latency for your users and keeping you informed.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

--- end draft ---

Internal asks: 
- Evelyn: can you approve the customer brief wording and the proposal to offer a one-week credit if we decide to apply the routing exception?
- Marissa/Karthik/Ben: please confirm when you flip the smoothing rule (Marissa said ~20m).
- Ben: please add a single-slide postmortem blurb for execs if we must escalate to credit.

Attachments: customer-briefing-draft-v2.md

Jasmine
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
